heading: INT. SHUTTERED BOWLING ALLEY - IMPROVISED ARBITRATION HALL - DAY

units.text: INT. SHUTTERED BOWLING ALLEY - IMPROVISED ARBITRATION HALL - DAY
Lanes polished to a dull glow.
A folding table placed at the foul line, three chairs, a pitcher of water.
Behind them, the pin deck, bare.
Dust floats in light from the high windows.
ARBITRATOR ODETTE MARCHAND, 60s, in a charcoal suit, sits at the head with a fountain pen and a legal pad.
She hasn't blinked in a minute.
COUNSEL ELLIOT VESPER, 40s, sleeves rolled, stands at the lane's edge with a stack of exhibits.
His client sits across from him: KHALID RAHMAN, 50s, a contractor's work boots and a clean white shirt, hands folded.
Mr. Rahman, you signed the original contract in March.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: Yes.
units.name: RAHMAN

units.text: And you understood that it covered the demolition and remediation of the east wing.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: I understood that it covered what I was told it covered.
units.name: RAHMAN

units.text: Told by whom?
units.name: VESPER

units.text: By you.
units.name: RAHMAN

units.text: Marchand's pen scratches.
Vesper smiles thinly.
Mr. Rahman, we have a signature on page nineteen.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: You have a signature on page nineteen. You do not have a signature on page twenty. Because page twenty does not exist.
units.name: RAHMAN

units.text: Vesper's smile stays.
His shoulders tighten.
Madam Arbitrator, the witness is characterizing.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: Overruled. Continue.
units.name: MARCHAND

units.text: Mr. Rahman. Is it your testimony that the contract was never finalized?
units.name: VESPER

units.text: It's my testimony that the contract you handed me was a draft, and the one you filed with this panel is a forgery.
units.name: RAHMAN

units.text: The word drops into the lane like a ball.
Nothing rolls.
Counsel, that is a serious accusation.
units.name: MARCHAND

units.text: Madam Arbitrator, I must --
units.name: VESPER

units.text: Seven years I have built hospitals. Seven. I have never once been accused of cutting corners. And you come here with a paper that says I did.
units.name: RAHMAN

units.text: Sit down, Mr. Rahman.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: I am sitting.
units.name: RAHMAN

units.text: Then be quiet.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: Or what?
units.name: RAHMAN

units.text: Vesper leans over the table, close.
Marchand puts down her pen with a click that rings off the pins.
Counsel. Step back.
units.name: MARCHAND

units.text: He steps back.
Slow.
He adjusts his cuffs, a tic.
Mr. Vesper. How long have you been practicing?
units.name: MARCHAND

units.text: Eighteen years.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: And in those eighteen years, have you ever once been handed a document that you knew to be incomplete?
units.name: MARCHAND

units.text: Never, Madam.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: Then why does the metadata on exhibit twelve show it was created on Tuesday?
units.name: MARCHAND

units.text: Vesper does not answer.
Rahman looks at him, then at the arbitrator, then at his own hands.
I did not want to say.
units.name: RAHMAN

units.text: Say it.
units.name: MARCHAND

units.text: I do not care about the money. I care that he is not ashamed.
units.name: RAHMAN

units.text: Marchand folds her hands.
The high windows glow.
A single bowling ball, stranded on the return rack, catches the light.
Mr. Vesper. I am suspending this hearing. I am referring exhibit twelve to the bar.
units.name: MARCHAND

units.text: Yes, Madam.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: He gathers his papers.
They shake.
The sound of paper is the loudest thing in the building.
